samples.summary: Revision-preview snapshot path recurses over the raw tree before `docsTreeToDocument`'s new nesting cap can apply
samples.evidence: `normalizeYsonTreeNode` (packages/frontend/src/components/history/snapshot-adapters.ts:123-143, recursive call at :140) walks the whole parsed snapshot tree with no depth bound and only then hands the result to `docsTreeToDocument` (:178), which is the reader the PR bounded with `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225). A `block > row > cell > block > table > …` chain written by a peer — precisely the hazard `model/table-nesting.ts:11` says no attribute band can reach — therefore overflows the stack in this pre-pass and throws a `RangeError` out of `parseDocsSnapshot`, so the version-history preview still crashes on the document the cap was added to keep openable. The cap protects the live store (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:480`) and the engine reader but not this consumer; the fix is a depth bound in `normalizeYsonTreeNode`. I could not confirm how deep a tree the server-stored snapshots can actually carry, hence low confidence, but the path is reachable from the preview UI.

finding.evidence: `normalizeYsonTreeNode` (packages/frontend/src/components/history/snapshot-adapters.ts:123-143, recursive call at :140) walks the whole parsed snapshot tree with no depth bound and only then hands the result to `docsTreeToDocument` (:178), which is the reader the PR bounded with `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225). A `block > row > cell > block > table > …` chain written by a peer — precisely the hazard `model/table-nesting.ts:11` says no attribute band can reach — therefore overflows the stack in this pre-pass and throws a `RangeError` out of `parseDocsSnapshot`, so the version-history preview still crashes on the document the cap was added to keep openable. The cap protects the live store (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:480`) and the engine reader but not this consumer; the fix is a depth bound in `normalizeYsonTreeNode`. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `normalizeYsonTreeNode` (packages/frontend/src/components/history/snapshot-adapters.ts:123-143) recurses over `node.children` at :140 with no depth parameter and no bound, and `parseDocsSnapshot` runs that full walk over the raw parsed tree at :178 before handing the materialised result to `docsTreeToDocument` — the reader that carries the cap (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225, MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH=32 at packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26). The cap therefore protects the engine reader and the live store (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:480) but not this consumer, whose pre-pass descends a peer-written `block > row > cell > block > table > …` chain unbounded. `unwrapYsonScalars` does not mitigate it: Tree-tagged aggregates are returned by reference (packages/frontend/src/components/history/unwrap-yson.ts:98), so the tree arrives intact. The path is reachable from the preview UI (packages/frontend/src/components/history/revision-preview.tsx:88, driven by the effect at :204-213). I considered refuting on `already-guarded` because the try/catch at revision-preview.tsx:212-221 converts a thrown RangeError into an error banner rather than a tab crash — so the finding's word "crashes" overstates the symptom — but that does not make it unreal or non-blocking: the cap exists specifically so such a document stays openable (degrading a too-deep table to a row-less one), and this consumer instead renders nothing but "could not be read". That is a guard whose protective intent does not hold at another consumer, squarely in the blast-radius lane. Caveat for the fixer, not affecting the verdict: YSON.parse at :174 must descend the same structure, so a bound in normalizeYsonTreeNode alone may be insufficient.

finding.summary: New read-side nesting cap has no matching write-side cap: a truncated table written back prunes the peer's deeper rows from the CRDT
finding.evidence: `treeNodeToBlock` now reads a table nested past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` as `rows: []` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:483, crdt-tree.ts:228), but the in-memory `Block` produced that way is the same object the write path serializes back: `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1680) does `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block))`, replacing the whole block subtree with what `buildBlockNode` (line 364/375) derives from `block.tableData.rows`. Any `doc.updateBlockDirect(...)` on an ancestor table (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4185, 4743) therefore rewrites the truncated shape into the tree and permanently deletes everything below level 32 for every peer. The backend writer has the same shape (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:150-200). Truncation-on-read is recoverable; truncation written back is not.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The read-side cap is real: yorkie-doc-store.ts:479-484 and crdt-tree.ts:223-229 return `rows: []` for any table at depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (table-nesting.ts:26). The write path has no matching cap: buildBlockNode (yorkie-doc-store.ts:364-376) serializes `block.tableData.rows` unconditionally, recursing through buildRowNode/buildCellNode (400-414) with no depth parameter, and YorkieDocStore.updateBlock (1666-1681) replaces the whole block subtree via `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block))`. A reachable caller round-trips the truncated model straight back into the tree: text-editor.ts:4721 reads the table via doc.getBlock (truncated reader output) and text-editor.ts:4743 writes it back via doc.updateBlockDirect -> document.ts:765-768 -> store.updateBlock; text-editor.ts:4185 is a second such site, and the whole-document rewrite at yorkie-doc-store.ts:3218-3267 has the same shape. No guard anywhere refuses to serialize a table that was truncated on read, so deeper rows written by a peer are permanently pruned from the CRDT rather than merely hidden — the opposite of the "degrade, do not vanish" invariant the cap's own comment states (table-nesting.ts:19-24). This is a contract change to a reader whose serializer/callers outside the diff were not updated: blast-radius lane, major impact (irrecoverable data loss on a reachable path).

finding.summary: DOCX import recurses into nested tables with no depth cap, so the producer the layout comment names can still overflow the stack and can create documents deeper than the reader will ever show
finding.evidence: `table-layout.ts`'s new comment says the layout bounds itself because "the layout takes documents from other producers too (DOCX import, paste)". That producer is `DocxImporter.convertTable`, which recurses unbounded at packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:415 (`cellBlocks.push(DocxImporter.convertTable(childEl, imageUrls))`) — a crafted .docx overflows the stack during import, before any layout runs, so the layout cap never sees it. A merely deep (say 40-level) import also succeeds, is written into the CRDT by the uncapped `buildBlockNode` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:375), and is then silently truncated to 32 on the next read. No cap exists on any producer side.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. `DocxImporter.convertTable` (packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:246) takes no depth parameter and re-enters itself unbounded at line 415 for nested `<w:tbl>` elements; a grep for depth/nesting/recursion across packages/docs/src/import finds only unrelated comments. The cap the layout comment references does exist (packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26, applied at packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:145 and at the frontend reader packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:480), but no producer-side cap covers DOCX import. I searched wide for a counterexample: paste IS capped (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:307/318/359 thread a depth), and the REST write path IS capped (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:438-447 vs MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH at :806) — but the browser DOCX import never passes either. Its chain is docx-actions.ts:31 -> upload-queue.ts:373,379 -> apply-imported-content.ts:224 (`store.setDocument`) -> writeFullDocument (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3207) -> buildBlockNode (yorkie-doc-store.ts:364-376), whose table branch maps rows with no depth at line 375 and writes directly into the CRDT, bypassing the backend validator. The CLI path (packages/cli/src/docs/docx-import.ts:74) is uncapped too. So a crafted .docx overflows the stack during parse before any cap runs, and a merely deep one is persisted then silently truncated to 32 on the next read. In lane for blast-radius: the diff introduces a nesting invariant enforced only at readers/layout while a named producer outside the diff violates it.

finding.summary: Sibling clamp on the model path still spreads row widths (`Math.max(0, ...rows.map(...))`) — the exact RangeError the new normalizeCellRange comment says it folded to avoid
finding.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts) now folds with `reduce` because "`Math.max(...rows)` throws `RangeError` past ~100k arguments, and the row count is a peer's to choose". The same computation on the model path was not changed: packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:57 does `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1`. Row count has no band (`numeric-attrs.ts` caps columns via `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS = 256` but nothing caps rows), so a peer-written table with >~125k rows makes this throw on every style apply / run visit that routes through `visitCellRectangleSlices` (range-runs.ts:81).

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists verbatim: packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:57 computes `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1`, spreading one argument per table row. Its sibling, packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:136-138, was changed to a `reduce` fold with an explicit comment (selection.ts:134-135) stating that `Math.max(...rows)` throws RangeError past ~100k arguments and that the row count is peer-chosen — so the repo itself documents the hazard and the model path was not brought along. Row count is genuinely unbounded: numeric-attrs.ts:95/256/380 caps columns at MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS=256, but bandOneBlock iterates table.rows (numeric-attrs.ts:383-384) with no cap, and no MAX_TABLE_ROWS exists anywhere in the repo. The site is reachable on live paths: Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells calls it at document.ts:700 (style write) and visitStyledRunsInRange at range-runs.ts:81 (toolbar summary/toggle read); neither bounds rows.length beforehand. This is an out-of-diff sibling site left out of step with the invariant the diff asserts, which is in the blast-radius lane, and the impact at that site is a thrown RangeError aborting the style apply/read. No guard, absence, or scope ground supports refutation.

finding.summary: Cell-rectangle loops on the raw (unnormalized) selection bypass the new normalizeCellRange clamp
finding.evidence: The new clamp lives only in `normalizeCellRange` (view/selection.ts), which runs on `getNormalizedRange`. Two hot consumers loop the raw `selection.range.tableCellRange` instead: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1791-1792 (`for (let r = minR; r <= maxR; r++)` over `range.tableCellRange` in `forEachBlockInSelection`) and packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2867-2868 (same shape). Neither clamps to `tableBlock.tableData.rows.length`, so an out-of-band rectangle spins exactly the way the diff's own rationale describes. Such a rectangle is reachable: `restoreSelectionFromPresence` carries `restoredSel.tableCellRange` verbatim into `selection.setRange` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2493) after validating only its `blockId`.

verdict.reason: The quoted raw loops do exist (editor.ts:1787-1799, text-editor.ts:2863-2875), but the claimed reachability of an out-of-band rectangle is wrong, so there is no reachable bypass of the new clamp. (1) Peer-written rectangles never reach the local Selection: a peer's activeSelection is copied into PeerCursor.selection (docs-view.tsx:257) and consumed only by computeSelectionRects at editor.ts:2094-2099, which goes through normalizeRange -> normalizeCellRange (selection.ts:181-195), i.e. the guarded path. (2) restoreSelectionFromPresence (editor.ts:2465-2466) reads the LOCAL client's own presence — getPresenceSelection is doc.getMyPresence() with a fallback to getPresenceForTest(local actorId) (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3365-3380), written by this client from its own selection (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1258, 3322-3334). It is not a peer-written value. (3) The only other external setter, EditorAPI.restoreLocalCursor (editor.ts:4576-4589), is called from docs-view.tsx:434-437 with resolveAnchoredLocalCursor(), which rebuilds tableCellRange from the locally recorded localSelectionAnchor (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1420-1424, set at 3426-3429). (4) Every production setRange carrying a tableCellRange derives it from layout/model-resolved cell addresses with existence checks (text-editor.ts:2393-2394/2413, 3967-3982, 3991-4000, 3322-3335), so indices are bounded by the table; a stale rectangle after a peer row deletion costs a handful of no-op iterations (rows[r]?.cells[c] -> continue), not the unbounded spin described. Remaining raw-vs-normalized divergence is a consistency nit, not a blocking guard bypass under this lens.
